business_scope.primary_industry_name: Maritime Seafarer Staffing and Vessel Crew Management Agency

meta_jurisdiction_context.jurisdiction_name_en: Colombia (unitary national jurisdiction; no sub-state corporate law distinction for the S.A.S. register)

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Ley 1258 de 2008 (Ley de Sociedades por Acciones Simplificadas), Arts. 1, 5, 12 and 28; Código de Comercio, Arts. 109, 110, 353 and 354; Decreto 2042 de 2014 (Registro Único Empresarial).
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Cámara de Comercio del domicilio social (Chamber of Commerce, via Registro Único Empresarial - RUES).
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Documento Privado de Constitución adjudicado ante notario o con autenticación de firma, radicado para inscripción en el Registro Mercantil.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum capital for S.A.S. under Ley 1258/2008. The by-laws may fix any subscribed amount; cash contributions must be deposited into a Colombian bank account opened in the entity's name prior to commercial registration. No escrow account is required by national law; the by-laws may set the payment schedule, but at least one third of subscribed cash capital must be paid if so provided in the by-laws.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED, that the incorporators and Sole Shareholder hereby subscribe to all issued shares of Sociedad por Acciones Simplificada, with aggregate par value as set forth in Exhibit A, and unanimously approve the by-laws presented to this meeting, which are declared binding. FURTHER RESOLVED, that the registered office is established at the address stated in the by-laws and shall be the seat of legal administration and receipt of official notices. FURTHER RESOLVED, that [Name] is appointed President and legal representative, [Name] is appointed Secretary, and [Name] is appointed fiscal auditor where required by law. Such appointments take effect immediately.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Corporate Name Availability Verification and Pre-Registration
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Cámara de Comercio de Bogotá or local Chamber of Commerce, through the RUES consultation platform (www.rues.com.co / ccb.org.co).
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit up to five proposed corporate names through the official 'consulta de homónimos' service to verify that no identical or confusingly similar name is already registered. Obtain the negative certification of name availability, which remains valid for thirty business days. This pre-validation is mandatory before drafting the incorporation document.
required_dossiers: Identification document (cédula or passport) of each incorporator or representative
List of proposed corporate names (max five)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is rejected or collides with an existing registration, the applicant must select the next available alternative from the submitted list and resubmit the query without additional payment; a formal appeal may be filed with the Chamber of Commerce if a name is refused incorrectly.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Execution of the Private Incorporation Document and By-laws
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Notary Public (authentication of signatures) or Chamber of Commerce authorized center for signature authentication.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Draft the Documento Privado de Constitución containing the complete by-laws, including corporate purpose, registered office, share subscription, capital structure, governance rules, and appointment of officers. Have all shareholders or their legal representatives execute the document, and authenticate each signature before a notary or authorized Chamber official. For corporate shareholders, provide board/entity approval and power of attorney.
required_dossiers: Draft private incorporation document and by-laws
Certified name availability certificate
Copies of shareholders' identification documents
Power of attorney if any shareholder acts through a representative
Corporate authorization if a legal entity is a shareholder
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the notary refuses authentication due to defects, correct the by-laws to comply with mandatory provisions, and if the Chamber rejects the document, file a corrected version within five business days or use a notarial public deed as an alternative instrument.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Opening of Corporate Bank Account and Capital Deposit
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Commercial bank authorized by the Financial Superintendence of Colombia (e.g., Bancolombia, Davivienda, BBVA Colombia) selected by the incorporators.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: With the execution copy of the incorporation document and the legal representative's identification, open a corporate bank account in the name of the S.A.S. Deposit the paid-up cash capital, or the portion required by the by-laws, and obtain a certificate of deposit or account summary evidencing that the funds are credited to the entity. This certificate must be presented during registration.
required_dossiers: Execution copy of the private incorporation document or notarial deed
Identity card and NIT (if already issued) of the legal representative
Bank account application form
Certificate of name availability and draft by-laws
DIAN provisional tax identification if required by the bank
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank requires a NIT before opening the account, obtain a temporary DIAN reference in the pre-registration stage or open the account under the 'cash capital deposit' procedure; if the bank rejects the documentation, submit corrected corporate documents and a revised board resolution to satisfy internal compliance.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Commercial Registration in the Registro Único Empresarial (RUES)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Cámara de Comercio con Jurisdicción en el Domicilio Social (Registro Mercantil).
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the fully executed private incorporation document, the capital deposit certificate, and any stamp tax (impuesto de timbre) payment with the local Chamber of Commerce. Complete the RUES registration form and pay the registration tariff. After formal verification of documents and the by-laws, the Chamber issues the Certificate of Registration and the Sistema de Información del Registro Mercantil entry. The S.A.S. exists in respect of third parties from this registration date.
required_dossiers: Signed and authenticated private incorporation document (or deed)
Certificate of paid-up capital deposit issued by the bank
Completed RUES registration form
Payment receipt of official registration tariff and stamp tax
Copies of shareholders' identification for registry data
Form of appointment of legal representative
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the registry issues a 'requerimiento' (query), the applicant must respond within five to ten business days, correct the specific defects in the by-laws or documentation, and resubmit. If registration is denied, a reconsideration appeal or appeal before the Chamber's administrative jurisdiction may be filed.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Tax and Sectoral Registration: NIT, RUT, and DIAN Filing
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: DIAN (Dirección de Impuestos y Aduanas Nacionales), through the MUISCA online portal.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After obtaining the Chamber of Commerce registration, request the Registro Único Tributario (RUT) by filing the corresponding form in MUISCA. The DIAN will assign or confirm the Número de Identificación Tributaria (NIT) and the company status. Provide the ISIC 5222 / NAICS 488390 activity classification (maritime crew recruitment and management services). This step finalizes the effective tax identity and permits the issuance of invoices and payroll operation.
required_dossiers: Certificate of incorporation issued by the Chamber of Commerce
Identification of the legal representative
Completed RUT form in the DIAN MUISCA portal
Definitive NIT assignment receipt
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the RUT filing is queried or rejected due to address, activity, or legal representative discrepancies, correct the online form and attach a scanned copy of the corrected Chamber registration. An in-person appointment at DIAN can be made to resolve persistent discrepancies, or an official appeal may be filed through MUISCA.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Dirección General Marítima (DIMAR), Ministry of National Defence, and the Ministry of Transport.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Permiso de Funcionamiento para Agencia de Reclutamiento y Contratación de Gente de Mar (Maritime Crew Recruitment Agency Operating Permit).

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Autoridad Nacional de Licencias Ambientales (ANLA) and the Regional Autonomous Corporation (CAR) having territorial jurisdiction.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exemption/Registration category — low-impact administrative office activity under CIIU 5222; no full EIA report required. Registration in the environmental control database and municipal environmental zoning certification are required.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Wastewater discharge to municipal sewer must meet Resolución 0631 de 2015 thresholds; office generation of hazardous waste (e-waste, batteries, cartridges) must be handled under Resolución 1402 de 2006; ambient noise and VOC emissions are limited to municipal urban standards; all solid waste must be disposed through authorized collectors in the Municipal Solid Waste Management Plan.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety measures require an inspection and certification from the Cuerpo de Bomberos of the local municipality; the office structural load and architectural safety must conform to NSR-10 earthquake resistant standards; workplace occupational health clearance is issued through the Administradora de Riesgos Laborales (ARL) and must include medical surveillance, fire evacuation drills, and appointment of a safety inspector under Resolution 0312 de 2019.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Dirección de Impuestos y Aduanas Nacionales (DIAN) - Official portal: https://www.dian.gov.co; transactional platform: https://muisca.dian.gov.co
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A foreign entity operating through a Colombian S.A.S. must obtain a Colombian NIT (Número de Identificación Tributaria) and register in the RUT (Registro Único Tributario). Procedure: (1) incorporate the S.A.S. before the local Chamber of Commerce (Cámara de Comercio); (2) appoint a legal representative resident in Colombia and obtain a corporate digital certificate/password; (3) apply for RUT inscription with DIAN either electronically through MUISCA or through a duly empowered attorney; (4) DIAN assigns the NIT and issues the RUT certificate; (5) request electronic invoicing authorization via DIAN by notifying the billing software or adopting the free DIAN billing system; (6) file an annual sworn statement of required information and designate a fiscal domicile for VAT and tax notifications.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Entity_Level_Taxation. A Colombian S.A.S. is a taxable legal entity subject to corporate-level taxation on worldwide income (standard 35% rate for income tax; dividends remitted to non-residents subject to additional withholding). It is treated as a Colombia tax resident because it is incorporated and effectively domiciled in Colombia; no partnership or pass-through classification is available.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: No check-the-box or pass-through election exists for S.A.S. under Colombian law. Statutory elections available include: (a) election to file consolidated income tax returns for qualifying economic groups (grupos empresariales) under Law 1819/2016 and Decree 1625/2016, subject to DIAN registration and 95% common control; (b) the Simplified Tax Regime (Régimen Simple de Tributación - SIMPLE) for small taxpayers with annual gross income at or below 3,500 UVT, which replaces and integrates income tax and VAT compliance; (c) for foreign investors, election to treat a Colombian permanent establishment (branch) as a separate taxpayer under the branch taxation regime; and (d) election to apply the participation exemption (holder exemption) to exempt 95% of qualifying domestic dividends from source taxation upon compliance with substance requirements.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: IVA (Impuesto sobre las Ventas) - Value Added Tax
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: Colombia does not establish a general economic turnover exemption for VAT registration; liability arises automatically for any person habitually performing taxable activities in Colombia, regardless of income volume, with a RUT registration duty from the first taxable act. For the simplified small-taxpayer regime, annual gross income must not exceed 3,500 UVT (approximately COP 164.7 million for 2024, at 1 UVT = COP 47,065), which permits a coupled VAT-income-tax filing through SIMPLE.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Electronic invoicing is mandatory for all Colombian VAT taxpayers. The invoice must be issued through DIAN-authorized software or the free DIAN system and transmitted in real time (or within DIAN-prescribed deadlines) in XML format, accompanied by the electronic invoice validation code (CUDS - Código Único de Facturación de Validación Electrónica DIAN), a digital signature certificate, and the seller's RUT validity verification. DIAN performs automatic validation before purchasers may receive the invoice as a deductible/cost instrument. Transactional information, software and hardware traceability records, and invoice batches must be accessible to DIAN, and electronic invoice authorization or the entire invoicing system may be suspended or penalized for noncompliance.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Zero-rated VAT (0%) applies to exports of goods and to qualifying export services rendered to non-resident parties, including maritime crew recruitment and vessel management services, when the service is physically delivered and consumed outside Colombian territory, the supplier holds a valid NIT and is registered in the RUT as an exporter, and the transaction is evidenced by commercial invoices, transport or delivery records, and foreign currency collection through the Colombian exchange market. Export documentation must demonstrate actual exit from Colombian customs territory or, in the case of services, that the recipient is abroad, the payment is made in hard currency, and no benefit or use occurs within Colombia.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (Declaración de Exportación) transmitted to DIAN and accepted per Colombian Customs Regulations
Commercial invoice (texto totalmente claro) identifying the exporter, importer, product description, amount, and zero-rated VAT indication
Bill of Lading or other transport document evidencing dispatch from Colombian port/airport and physical exit of the goods
Packing list and freight/cargo manifest (when applicable)
Inward Remittance Certificate (Certificado de Reintegro Cambiario) or sworn bank statement issued by the Colombian commercial bank evidencing receipt of export proceeds in foreign currency
RUT certificate and exporter authorization issued by DIAN
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: DIAN may retroactively disallow zero-rating refunds and VAT credits when export documentation is incomplete, the export declaration differs from actual exit data, proceeds are not repatriated within the 180-day statutory deadline, or underlying services are considered used in Colombia. Tax clawbacks carry default interest (current lending rate plus three percentage points), and fines may reach 160% of the tax evaded, plus a late-filing/sanction penalty of up to COP 20 million or more. False or fraudulent export declarations used to obtain VAT refunds or warrants for found guilty of unjustified tax benefit, criminal liability may attach under Article 402 of the Colombian Criminal Code on fraud against tax administration, including imprisonment and monetary sanctions. Supporting records must be preserved for at least six years from the export declaration date.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banco de la República de Colombia (Central Bank of Colombia), with the Superintendencia Financiera de Colombia as supervisory arm; foreign-exchange regime (Régimen de Cambios Internacionales) codified under Ley 9 de 1991, Decreto 1735 de 1993 and Resolución 2016006416 (Circular Reglamentaria DCIN-83).
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Current-account transactions, including maritime crew-placement and vessel-management service fees classified as service exports, are freely convertible but must be routed through an authorized exchange-market intermediary (IMC). Capital-account operations (equity injections, shareholder loans) do not require prior FX approval but mandate channeling through an IMC and registration with Banco de la República as a precondition for lawful dividend or capital repatriation. Profit-remittance hurdles: verified payment of 35% corporate income tax, dividend withholding at source under E.T. Articles 242/245, registration of the underlying foreign investment, and submission of Declaración de Cambio Formulario No. 1 at each remittance via the IMC. Unregistered foreign investment renders remittances illicit and subject to exchange penalties.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Export proceeds derived from services (crewing fees, management fees) must be channeled to Colombia through an IMC within six (6) months from invoice or service-completion date where the individual transaction exceeds USD 10,000 or the monthly aggregate exceeds USD 10,000. The channeling obligation applies to 100% of the invoiced export value; no partial surrender ratio exists. Proceeds may be retained in foreign currency in a permitted FX-denominated account at the IMC without mandatory conversion to COP; repatriated foreign currency may not be left outside the Colombian financial system beyond the statutory term. Non-compliance triggers exchange fines (multas cambiarias) imposed by the Banco de la República and DIAN, and may render future FX authorizations unavailable.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Operational Account (Cuenta Corriente en Moneda Legal) with linked Multi-Currency Foreign Exchange Account (Cuenta en Moneda Extranjera)
Operational Account with FX desk and International Trade Settlement module
Operational Account (non-denominated COP) with Foreign-Currency Account for export proceeds
Operational Account with Multi-Currency Payroll and SWIFT Corporate Access
Operational Account with USD Nostro-Vostro coverage for crew payroll corridors

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Low. Offshore e-money institutions (Wise, Payoneer, Airwallex) are not registered IMCs under Colombia's exchange regime; they cannot lawfully intermediate receipt of export proceeds and their use for crew-placement fee collection would breach the mandatory channeling obligation. Such EMIs are tolerable only for ancillary outbound disbursements (e.g., SaaS subscriptions, marketing tools) and must never aggregate seafarer payroll funding or shipowner receivables. Any persistent lateral flows between an offshore EMI and a Colombian IMC account will trigger enhanced due diligence and potential account suspension.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Physical branch appearance of the legal representative or a locally appointed attorney-in-fact holding a notarized and apostilled power of attorney is mandatory for corporate account opening at all tier-1 Colombian banks. Video-call interviews may serve only as supplementary KYC evidence, not as a substitute for the in-person identity verification of the signatory. Non-resident shareholders must be identified through chamber-certified corporate documents, valid passports, the RUT, and the Beneficial Ownership Registry (Registro de Beneficiarios Finales) declaration. Boards must issue a specific treasury-mandate resolution identifying account signatories and approved FX hedging limits.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Payments received from shipowners, operators, or charterers associated with OFAC/EU/UK sanctioned jurisdictions, or from non-transparent bareboat and shadow-fleet charter structures.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Vessel IMO number and flag-state registration certificate; OFAC/EU/UK consolidated sanctions screening reports per counterparty; charter-party and ship-management agreements; beneficial-ownership declarations of each foreign counterparty; DIMAR-issued manning-agency license; completed counterparty KYC questionnaire.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-volume multi-currency payroll to seafarers of multiple nationalities presenting trade-servitude or wage-laundering red flags.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Individual Seafarer Employment Agreements (SEA) aligned with ITF salary scales; valid Seafarer Identity Documents and passports; flag-state endorsed crew lists; per-vessel and per-month payroll registers; SWIFT MT103 trails linking each wage payment to the corresponding SEA and the vessel deployment schedule.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: S.A.S. with 100% non-resident shareholders and rapid in-and-out treasury flows lacking local substance.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Cámara de Comercio Certificate of Existence and Representation; RUT; Registry of Final Beneficiaries filings; board minutes approving bank account opening and treasury mandates; audited financial statements; Colombian office lease agreement; payroll and operational contact materials evidencing local management substance.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Interposition of third-party sub-agents or intermediate manning brokers in the commission and wage disbursement chain.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Master agency and sub-manning agreements; statutory licenses of each sub-agent under flag-state crewing regulations; documented delegation chain; transaction-ledger reconciliations; anti-sanctions and anti-money-laundering warranties executed by each intermediate counterparty.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Equity injections from non-resident shareholders must be sent via SWIFT MT103 to the S.A.S. account at a Colombian IMC with a precise payment purpose ('Aporte de capital social en moneda extranjera'), full investor identification, and simultaneous registration in the Banco de la República foreign-investment registry through the IMC (Declaración de Cambio por Inversión Internacional). Registration is a condition precedent for future dividend remittances or capital reimbursement; the IMC issues the exchange registration certificate evidencing valid foreign investment status. Shareholder loans must be documented with loan agreements and submitted under the respective foreign-debt concept code to avoid recharacterization as taxable equity.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Primary clearing rail is SWIFT MT103 for seafarer wage payments and overseas sub-agent fees in USD, EUR, or GBP; COP-denominated payroll is cleared through the local ACH platform (CENIT) with same-day or next-day value. Bulk multi-currency payroll is executed via the IMC's corporate payroll module with an itemized MT103 batch for each beneficiary. Commercial letters of credit (UCP600) are used only for procurement of vessel stores, safety equipment, or insured supplies, and must be issued by the same IMC to maintain a clean documentary audit trail. All outbound transfers require an associated exchange declaration voucher (Declaración de Cambio Formulario No. 1 or supporting form) to evidence permissible FX purpose.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Deliverable FX forwards on USD/COP and EUR/COP executed through an IMC, subject to documentary proof of underlying crew-payroll or crewing-fee exposure.

Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) on USD/COP permitted only where the IMC quotes an offshore-style non-deliverable structure and the S.A.S. demonstrates a genuine hedging need; onshore deliverable forwards are preferred for compliance simplicity.
FX swaps (spot/forward combinations and overnight rollover swaps) used to manage liquidity timing mismatches between shipowner receivables and multi-currency payroll runs.

Vanilla FX options and zero-cost collars for protecting the S.A.S. operating margin against adverse COP revaluation; cross-currency swaps are admissible only when matched to a specific long-term asset or liability exposure and documented under ISDA or the IMC's master derivatives agreement.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Commercial Registry Renewal (Renovación de la Matrícula Mercantil / RUE)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Chamber of Commerce where the S.A.S. maintains its principal registration (Cámara de Comercio)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually by 31 March for the preceding fiscal year; calendar companies with any registered activity must renew at all registries before the close of the same day
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late renewal triggers an escalating arrears fine (surcharge on the registration tariff) and administrative warning; continued non-renewal in the same year can lead to suspension of the commercial registration, loss of ability to file RUT updates and execute exempt operations, and eventual administrative strike-off of the merchant record.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Financial Statements: Certification, Shareholder Approval, and Deposit at the Commercial Registry
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Chamber of Commerce (filed jointly with the annual renewal); copy available to the Superintendence of Companies (Superintendencia de Sociedades) where so required
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: No later than 31 March of the year following the financial year-end; this is aligned with the commercial registry renewal window and not a separate extension
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to file the approved financial statements blocks the commercial-registry renewal, exposes the company to corporate-registry penalties, and may trigger a formal inspection by the Superintendence of Companies.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Final Beneficiary / UBO Report (Declaración Anual de Beneficiarios Finales)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: DIAN – Registro Único de Beneficiarios Finales (RUBF)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually within the calendar window published by DIAN (generally early May of the following year); the exact deadline depends on the last digit category assigned to the company's NIT
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Omission or inaccurate report can attract monetary fines per false or missing shareholder identification, adverse RUT enforcement actions, and impediments to obtain certificates of compliance and/or operate as a registered maritime crew recruiter.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Corporate Income Tax Return (Declaración de Renta y Complementario)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: DIAN (Unidad Administrativa Especial Dirección de Impuestos y Aduanas Nacionales)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually filed in the August-September national calendar; the due date is set by the last two digits of the NIT and is mandatory regardless of net taxable income
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing carries an extemporaneity penalty of 5% of the tax payable for each full or partial month of delay, capped at 100% of the tax liability, plus default interest; non-filing can trigger formal liquidation and criminal exposure.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Transfer Pricing Informative Return (Declaración Informativa de Precios de Transferencia)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Same annual NIT-driven income tax return deadline, applicable only where the S.A.S. exceeds the statutory thresholds and carries out controlled transactions with abroad-related parties (including crew-agency service invoicing to foreign shipowners)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failures to file or unfounded reporting can impose a specific penalty of up to 2,100 UVT in addition to adjustment of considered omitted income and tax settlements.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: A S.A.S. must appoint a certified Revisor Fiscal (statutory auditor) where: (a) the company has a gross income or gross assets equal to or exceeding 20,000 Tax Value Units (UVT) in the immediately preceding year; (b) the company is a controlling or controlled entity of a business group; (c) the Superintendence of Companies or special maritime rules so mandate; (d) the shareholders' agreement or company bylaws require an auditor; or (e) the company is engaged in public-interest or licensed regulated activities that trigger supervisory audit requirements. A maritime crew recruiter holding an authorization from the national maritime authority must additionally satisfy any DIMAR/Maritime Directorate audit condition attached to the crew-recruitment license.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: IFRS as issued by the IASB and incorporated into Colombia, or IFRS for SMEs for small and medium-sized entities when the S.A.S. is classified by the Superintendence of Companies in the SME segment; normative source: Decree 2420 of 2015 and its updating decrees.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Annually before or at the commercial registry renewal date, the S.A.S. must review and confirm its complete chain of ownership to identify every natural-person final beneficiary. The annual RUBF disclosure to DIAN must state any natural persons directly or indirectly holding 10% or more of shares/control, persons exercising final control through other means, and must declare a 'negative confirmation' where no natural-person UBO exists. Any share transfer occurring during the year must be reflected in the shareholders' register and in the RUT before the next annual confirmation.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Members / Shareholders (Libro de Registro de Accionistas)
Register of Directors and Board of Directors Minutes (Libro de Actas de Junta Directiva)
Shareholders' Meeting Minutes Book (Libro de Actas de Asamblea de Accionistas)
Final Beneficial Owners internal file supporting the annual RUBF declaration
Financial statements and supporting accounting vouchers required under Colombian commercial and IFRS retention rules

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: No statutory tax holiday applies to crew recruitment activities; the entity is subject to the full 35% corporate income tax. An incremental 25% deduction for qualifying science, technology and innovation (CTeI) expenses may lower the effective rate, but no additional preferential rate is available for ship crew recruitment.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Formulario 210 – Declaración de Renta y Complementario para Personas Jurídicas y Asimiladas; filed electronically through DIAN's Virtual Platform (Muisca) at www.dian.gov.co
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: On or before the exact date set by DIAN's annual taxpayer calendar, typically between the first week of April and the last week of June following the fiscal year-end. The date is determined by the last two digits of the taxpayer's NIT.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: NIT (Número de Identificación Tributaria) of the SAS.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: For the Colombian S.A.S., enter the Colombian tax ID. Do not enter foreign shareholder identifiers.
Always the full calendar year (January 1 – December 31), regardless of ownership.

Include all Colombian-source revenue from ship crew recruitment and management services; foreign-source income is also taxable for a Colombian resident entity but is declared separately in complementary boxes.
Claim only verifiable payroll costs, licenses, insurance, and administrative expenses. Cross-border inter-company payments must be arm's length and contemporaneously documented.
Result after costs, deductions and loss carryforwards; cannot be reduced by dividends paid to shareholders.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxable income before application of preferential rates (renta líquida gravable).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: For a standard SAS, this is the final income to be taxed at 35%.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Income tax payable (impuesto sobre la renta).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Amount due, after withholding credits, if any. Full payment must be remitted by the filing deadline.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late submission penalty: 5% of the tax due for each month or fraction of delay, up to a maximum of 100% of the tax. Late payment: monthly default interest at the central-bank rate plus a 10% surcharge. Non-filing without a request can trigger DIAN's automatic assessment and additional penalties for sending the return late after a request (sanción por no enviar información).

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 10% statutory withholding tax on dividends paid to non-resident beneficiaries where the profits out of which the dividend is paid have been taxed at corporate level. Dividends paid out of untaxed (exempt) profits are subject to an additional complementary income tax assessment of up to 35% on the shareholder.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To claim a reduced withholding tax rate under a Double Taxation Agreement (DTA), the non-resident shareholder must provide the Colombian paying entity with: (i) a Tax Residency Certificate (TRC) issued by the foreign tax authority; (ii) a statement of beneficial ownership; and (iii) a written request for the applicable treaty rate. These documents must be translated into Spanish and, where required, apostilled or legalised. The paying entity applies the reduced rate and retains a file record; a refund of excess WHT can be claimed through DIAN within the respective statute of limitations if the documentation is accepted only after payment.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Interest — statutory WHT rate of 20% (commonly reduced to 10%–15% under DTAs). Royalties for the use of industrial patents, trademarks or IP — statutory WHT rate of 30% (reduced in many treaties to 10%–15%). Technical assistance or service fees may be subject to WHT of 20% and, if not structured as a royalty, may be treated as normal service income subject to standard 35% corporate tax if attributable to a Colombian permanent establishment.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Local File (Basic) and Master File (if group revenue exceeds USD 50 million) are mandatory when the Colombian taxpayer's gross income or total assets exceed approximately COP 5.4 billion (≈ USD 1.3 million, equivalent to 135,000 UVT for fiscal 2024) and aggregate related-party cross-border transactions surpass approximately COP 120 million (≈ USD 27,000, corresponding to 3,000 UVT). These thresholds are annually adjusted by UVT.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Colombia does not apply offshore Economic Substance Regulations (ESR). Nevertheless, transfer pricing adjustments, GAAR and substance-over-form doctrines require the S.A.S. to evidence real management and control—actual office, employed staff, payroll and account management—in Colombia. A pure 'shell' or 'letterbox' entity is disregardable; its intercompany transactions may be recharacterised, and treaty benefits denied on beneficial ownership grounds.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Intentionally omitting crew-recruitment gross income (e.g., using offshore invoicing), inflating salary deductions for personnel never engaged, or fabricating invoices to artificially lower the 35% CIT base.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Administrative penalty equal to 100% of the evaded tax plus default interest; criminal prosecution under Article 339A of the Colombian Criminal Code carries imprisonment of 5 to 15 years for fraudulent evasion exceeding 2,500 UVT.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who sign fraudulent returns or direct the concealment are jointly, severally and personally liable for the full tax debt; they face criminal conviction, asset freezing/seizure, arrest warrants, travel bans, and suspension of commercial or administrative rights for up to 10 years.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Operating the S.A.S. as a mere payroll- or invoice-conduit with no Colombian office, management, or real crew-placement activity, while diverting profits to related parties in low-tax territories.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: DIAN may disregard the legal form, reattribute profits to the true economic operator, impose a 160% penalty on the understated tax attributable to aggressive planning, and cancel the NIT; additional OECD BEPS Action 6 penalties for treaty abuse may be asserted.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Colombian court jurisprudence permits piercing the corporate veil when the entity is used as a tool for fraud; directors may be condemned to repay the entire tax debt, disqualified from managing companies, and criminally sanctioned if the shell structure facilitates money laundering.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Engaging in multi-currency crew payroll and swift-wire transfers without establishing a risk management system: no KYC for shipowners or seafarers, no reporting of suspicious payroll movements to the UIAF for transactions ≥ COP 25 million, or processing funds for designated sanctions targets.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Administrative sanctions under Law 1766 of 2020 and regulatory decrees: fines of up to COP 1.2 billion for corporate AML breaches plus license revocation by the Ministry of Transportation (maritime crew agencies). Money laundering (Criminal Code Art. 323) carries 10 to 20 years of prison and fines up to 50,000 minimum monthly wages.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and compliance officers are personally and criminally liable if they knew or should have known of unauthorised wire transfers. Criminal penalties include 10–20 years' imprisonment, personal financial liability, travel limitations and forfeiture of assets.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failing to withhold the 10% dividend WHT on outbound remittances to non-resident shareholders, or improperly applying treaty reductions without obtaining a valid TRC and beneficial-ownership declaration.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: A fine equal to 100% of the sum not withheld, plus default interest; each late month adds a 1.5% penalty. The tax agent (the S.A.S.) remains liable to DIAN for the unrecovered sum. Repeated violations may also block future dividend remittances from the Central Bank exchange system.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Legal representatives are personally liable as retention agents; where omission is intentional, the director may be charged with criminal retention misappropriation (Art. 402 Criminal Code), punishable by up to 9 years in prison, disqualification from holding public or corporate office, and travel bans.
